title: [YouPass Collect] - Retirement age by gender across countries

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the average age at which men and women retired in six different countries in 2003.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, Korea recorded the highest retirement age for both genders, while France and Italy had the lowest figures. In addition, across all six nations, men retired later than women.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding countries with higher retirement ages, Korean men retired at 68 years and 8 months, the highest figure among all nations, followed by Japanese men at 67 years and 4 months. Meanwhile, men in the United States and Australia stopped working at 65 years 6 months and 64 years 1 month, respectively. As for women, they showed a similar pattern, with Korean females retiring at 67 years and 2 months, slightly ahead of their Japanese counterparts at 66 years and 9 months. The figures for American and Australian women were lower, at 64 years 2 months and 63 years 5 months, in that order.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to countries with lower retirement ages, Italian men left the workforce at 58 years and 2 months, marginally higher than French men at 57 years and 4 months. Similarly, women in Italy retired at 57 years and 3 months, compared to 56 years and 9 months for their French counterparts, marking the lowest retirement age among all countries examined.
